text:
From highest to lowest, U.S. law runs: the U.S. Constitution; federal treaties and statutes, which are coequal (the later-in-time one prevails when they conflict); federal regulations; then state constitutions, state statutes, state regulations, and local ordinances. Under the Supremacy Clause (Article VI), valid federal law overrides conflicting state law at every level. The list is a simplification: state constitutions and statutes don't rank strictly below federal regulations, since each sits within its own domain, and common law and case precedent operate alongside these sources rather than in a fixed slot.

CONFIDENCE: 85
